newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul chip shrs largely unmoved by output cut news.
newsitem.headline: Seoul chip shrs largely unmoved by output cut news.

text.p: Shares of South Korean chipmakers were mixed in Thursday afternoon trading, unmoved by news that chipmakers would cut production of dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, brokers said.
Samsung Electronics Co and LG Semicon Co were each up 100 won to 47,200 and 20,200, respectively. But Hyundai Electronics Industries Co shed 200 won to 24,400.
Samsung, the largest of the three, said it would further cut production of 16-megabit DRAMs due to worsening profitability as a result of low prices.
"Investors think it's too early to say the production cut will immediately lead to a recovery in the prices," said Lee Gyu-bum, an analyst at Hyundai Securities.

Earlier, the U.S. unit of LG Semicon said the company had decided to shift some manufacturing resources out of 16-megabit DRAMs production, which could result "over a period of time" in reducing its 16-megabit DRAMs output.
